title: KCET 2024 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A2

questions.q: The type of linkage present between nucleotides is
questions.explanation: Nucleotides in nucleic acids are joined together by phosphodiester linkages between the 3' and 5' carbons of adjacent sugar units.

questions.q: $\alpha$-D-(+)-glucose and $\beta$-D-(+)-glucose are
questions.explanation: They differ only in configuration at C1 (the anomeric carbon), so they are called anomers.

questions.q: Propanone and Propanal are
questions.explanation: Propanone (a ketone) and propanal (an aldehyde) share the molecular formula C$_3$H$_6$O but have different functional groups, so they are functional isomers.

questions.q: Sodium ethanoate on heating with soda lime gives 'X'. Electrolysis of aqueous solution of sodium ethanoate gives 'Y'. 'X' and 'Y' respectively are
questions.explanation: CH$_3$COONa with soda lime undergoes decarboxylation to give CH$_4$ (X); Kolbe electrolysis of aqueous CH$_3$COONa gives C$_2$H$_6$ (Y) at the anode.

questions.q: But-1-yne on reaction with dil. H$_2$SO$_4$ in presence of Hg$^{2+}$ ions at 333 K gives [structures shown: (A) butan-2-one CH$_3$COCH$_2$CH$_3$; (B) butanal CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$CHO; (C) but-3-en-2-one CH$_2$=CHCOCH$_3$; (D) but-3-enal CH$_2$=CHCH$_2$CHO]
questions.explanation: Hg$^{2+}$-catalysed Markovnikov hydration of the terminal alkyne but-1-yne gives an enol that tautomerises to the ketone butan-2-one.

questions.q: Biologically active adrenaline and ephedrine used to increase blood pressure contain
questions.explanation: Both adrenaline and ephedrine contain an N-CH$_3$ secondary amino group.

questions.q: In the reaction Aniline $\xrightarrow{NaNO_2/dil.HCl}$ P $\xrightarrow{Phenol/NaOH}$ Q, Q is
questions.explanation: Aniline is diazotised to benzenediazonium chloride (P), which undergoes azo coupling with phenol at the para position to give para-hydroxyazobenzene (Q).

questions.q: The female sex hormone which is responsible for the development of secondary female characteristics and participates in the control of menstrual cycle is
questions.explanation: Estradiol is the principal female sex hormone regulating secondary sexual characteristics and the menstrual cycle.

questions.q: In the following scheme of reactions: C$_2$H$_5$Cl $\xrightarrow{X}$ C$_2$H$_5$F; C$_2$H$_5$Cl $\xrightarrow{Y}$ CH$_2$=CH$_2$; C$_2$H$_5$Cl $\xrightarrow{Z}$ C$_4$H$_{10}$. X, Y and Z respectively are:
options: HF, aqueous KOH and Na in dry ether
Hg$_2$F$_2$, alcoholic KOH and Na in dry ether
questions.explanation: Hg$_2$F$_2$ converts C$_2$H$_5$Cl to C$_2$H$_5$F (Swarts reaction); alcoholic KOH causes dehydrohalogenation to ethene; Na in dry ether gives the Wurtz coupling product butane.

questions.q: 8.8 g of monohydric alcohol added to ethyl magnesium iodide in ether liberates 2240 cm$^3$ of ethane at STP. This monohydric alcohol when oxidised using pyridinium chlorochromate forms a carbonyl compound that answers silver mirror test (Tollen's test). The monohydric alcohol is
questions.explanation: Moles of ethane = 2240/22400 = 0.1 mol = moles of alcohol, so molar mass = 8.8/0.1 = 88 g/mol, matching 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol, a primary alcohol whose PCC oxidation gives an aldehyde (positive Tollens' test).

questions.q: When a tertiary alcohol 'A' (C$_4$H$_{10}$O) reacts with 20% H$_3$PO$_4$ at 358 K, it gives a compound 'B' (C$_4$H$_8$) as a major product. The IUPAC name of the compound 'B' is
questions.explanation: Acid-catalysed dehydration of tert-butanol (2-methylpropan-2-ol) can give only 2-methylpropene as the alkene product.

questions.q: PCC is
options: A complex of chromium trioxide with pyridine + HCl
questions.explanation: Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is the complex formed from chromium trioxide, pyridine and HCl.

questions.q: On treating 100 mL of 0.1 M aqueous solution of the complex CrCl$_3$.6H$_2$O with excess of AgNO$_3$, 2.86 g of AgCl was obtained. The complex is
questions.explanation: 0.01 mol of complex gives 0.02 mol AgCl (2.86 g / 143.5 g mol$^{-1}$), so 2 Cl$^-$ ions are ionisable, giving the formula [Cr(H$_2$O)$_5$Cl]Cl$_2$.H$_2$O.

questions.q: The complex compounds [Co(NH$_3$)$_5$SO$_4$]Br and [Co(NH$_3$)$_5$Br]SO$_4$ are
questions.explanation: They differ in which ion (Br$^-$ or SO$_4^{2-}$) lies inside versus outside the coordination sphere, which is the defining feature of ionisation isomerism.

questions.q: When of the following statements are true about [CoF$_6$]$^{3-}$ ion? I) The complex has octahedral geometry. II) Coordination number of Co is 3 and oxidation state is +6. III) The complex is sp$^3$d$^2$ hybridised. IV) It is a high spin complex.
questions.explanation: [CoF$_6$]$^{3-}$ is octahedral (I) with Co in the +3 state and coordination number 6 (so II is false); the weak-field F$^-$ ligand gives an sp$^3$d$^2$ hybridised, high-spin complex (III and IV true).

questions.q: A haloalkane undergoes S$_N$2 or S$_N$1 reaction depending on
questions.explanation: The polarity and ionising power of the solvent determine whether substitution proceeds via the S$_N$1 or S$_N$2 pathway.

questions.q: 2-Methyl propane can be prepared by Wurtz reaction. The haloalkanes taken along with metallic sodium and dry ether are:
questions.explanation: Wurtz coupling of chloromethane and 2-chloropropane with Na/dry ether gives 2-methylpropane.

questions.q: In the analysis of III group basic radicals of salts, the purpose of adding NH$_4$Cl$_{(s)}$ to NH$_4$OH is:
options: to increase the concentration of OH$^-$ ions.
to precipitate the radicals of group IV and V.
to suppress the dissociation of NH$_4$OH.
questions.explanation: NH$_4$Cl provides NH$_4^+$ ions which, by the common ion effect, suppress the dissociation of NH$_4$OH so that only group III hydroxides are precipitated.

questions.q: Solubility product of CaC$_2$O$_4$ at a given temperature in pure water is $4\times10^{-9}$ (mol L$^{-1}$)$^2$. Solubility of CaC$_2$O$_4$ at the same temperature is
In the reaction between moist SO$_2$ and acidified permanganate solution:
options: SO$_2$ is oxidised to SO$_4^{2-}$; MnO$_4^-$ is reduced to Mn$^{2+}$
SO$_2$ is reduced to S; MnO$_4^-$ is oxidised to MnO$_4$
SO$_2$ is oxidised to SO$_3^{2-}$; MnO$_4^-$ is reduced to MnO$_2$
SO$_2$ is reduced to H$_2$S; MnO$_4^-$ is oxidised to MnO$_4$
questions.explanation: 2MnO$_4^-$ + 5SO$_2$ + 2H$_2$O $\rightarrow$ 2Mn$^{2+}$ + 5SO$_4^{2-}$ + 4H$^+$: permanganate is reduced to Mn$^{2+}$ while SO$_2$ is oxidised to sulfate.

questions.q: Which one of the following properties is generally not applicable to ionic hydrides?
questions.explanation: Ionic hydrides are high-melting, crystalline solids and are non-volatile, so 'volatile' does not apply to them.

questions.q: Which one of the following nitrates will decompose to give NO$_2$ on heating?
questions.explanation: Due to its small size and high polarising power, LiNO$_3$ decomposes like alkaline earth nitrates to give Li$_2$O, NO$_2$ and O$_2$, unlike the other alkali metal nitrates which give nitrites.

questions.q: Which of the following halides cannot be hydrolysed?
questions.explanation: Carbon has no available d-orbitals to expand its octet and accept a nucleophile, so CCl$_4$ resists hydrolysis, unlike SiCl$_4$, GeCl$_4$ and SnCl$_4$.

questions.q: 0.48 g of an organic compound on complete combustion produced 0.22 g of CO$_2$. The percentage of C in the given organic compound is:
questions.explanation: %C = (12/44) $\times$ (mass of CO$_2$/mass of compound) $\times$ 100 = (12/44) $\times$ (0.22/0.48) $\times$ 100 = 12.5%.

questions.q: In the given sequence of reactions, identify 'P', 'Q' and 'S' respectively. CH$_2$=CH$_2$ $\xrightarrow{P}$ CH$_2$Br-CH$_2$Br $\xrightarrow{Q}$ CH$_2$=CH-Br; also CH$_2$=CH-Br $\xrightarrow{R}$ CH$\equiv$CH $\xrightarrow{S}$ C$_6$H$_6$
options: HBr, Alc.KOH, NaNH$_2$, Red hot iron tube
Br$_2$, Alc.KOH, NaNH$_2$, Red hot iron tube
questions.explanation: Ethene adds Br$_2$ to give 1,2-dibromoethane (P = Br$_2$), which on dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic KOH (Q) gives bromoethene; NaNH$_2$ then gives acetylene, which cyclotrimerises over a red-hot iron tube (S) to give benzene.

questions.q: The first chlorinated organic insecticide prepared is:
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: DDT (dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) was the first synthetic chlorinated organic insecticide.

questions.q: Vapour pressure of a solution containing 18 g of glucose and 178.2 g of water at 100°C is: (Vapour pressure of pure water at 100°C = 760 torr)
questions.explanation: n(water) = 9.9, n(glucose) = 0.1, mole fraction of glucose = 0.1/10 = 0.01; ($P_0-P_s$)/$P_0$ = 0.01 gives $P_s$ $\approx$ 752.0 torr.

questions.q: A mixture of phenol and aniline shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. This is due to the formation of:
questions.explanation: Phenol and aniline form an intermolecular hydrogen bond between -OH and -NH$_2$ groups, strengthening attractions and lowering the vapour pressure below the ideal value.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs will show positive deviation from Raoult's Law?
questions.explanation: Benzene disrupts the hydrogen-bonded structure of methanol without forming comparably strong new interactions, weakening intermolecular forces and giving a positive deviation.

questions.q: How many Coulombs are required to oxidise 0.1 mole of H$_2$O to oxygen?
questions.explanation: H$_2$O $\rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{2}$O$_2$ + 2H$^+$ + 2e$^-$ needs 2 Faradays per mole; for 0.1 mol, charge = 0.1 $\times$ 2 $\times$ 96500 = $1.93\times10^4$ C.

questions.q: A current of 3A is passed through a molten calcium salt for 1 hr 47 min 13 sec. The mass of calcium deposited is: (Molar mass of Ca = 40 g mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: Time = 6433 s; charge = 3 $\times$ 6433 = 19299 C $\approx$ 0.2 mol electrons; since Ca$^{2+}$ + 2e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ Ca, moles of Ca = 0.1, mass = 0.1 $\times$ 40 = 4.0 g.

questions.q: The value of 'A' in the equation $\lambda_m = \lambda_m^0 - A\sqrt{C}$ is the same for the pair
questions.explanation: The Kohlrausch constant 'A' depends on the charge (valence) type of the electrolyte; NaCl and KBr are both 1:1 electrolytes and so share the same 'A'.

questions.q: For the reaction A $\rightleftharpoons$ B, E$_a$ = 50 kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $\Delta H$ = -20 kJ mol$^{-1}$. When a catalyst is added, E$_a$ decreases by 10 kJ mol$^{-1}$. What is the E$_a$ for the backward reaction in the presence of catalyst?
questions.explanation: $\Delta H = (E_a)_f - (E_a)_b$; with the catalyst $(E_a)_f = 40$, so $-20 = 40 - (E_a)_b$, giving $(E_a)_b = 60$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.

questions.q: For the reaction PCl$_5$ $\rightarrow$ PCl$_3$ + Cl$_2$, rate and rate constant are $1.02\times10^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$s$^{-1}$ and $3.4\times10^{-5}$s$^{-1}$ respectively at a given instant. The molar concentration of PCl$_5$ at that instant is:
Which one of the following does not represent Arrhenius equation?
questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation has a negative exponent, $k=Ae^{-E_a/RT}$; option D has the sign reversed and so does not represent it.

questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:
options: Oxides of nitrogen in the atmosphere can cause depletion of the ozone layer
Ozone absorbs the intense ultraviolet radiation of Sun
Depletion of ozone layer is because of its chemical reactions with chlorofluoro alkanes
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Ozone absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation, not infrared radiation, so statement D is incorrect.

questions.q: The transition element ($\approx$5%) present with lanthanoid metal in Misch metal is
questions.explanation: Misch metal is about 95% lanthanoid metal and about 5% iron.

questions.q: Match the following: I. Zn$^{2+}$, II. Cu$^{2+}$, III. Ni$^{2+}$ with i. d$^8$ configuration, ii. Colourless, iii. $\mu$ = 1.73 BM. Codes:
questions.explanation: Zn$^{2+}$ (d$^{10}$) is colourless (ii); Cu$^{2+}$ (d$^9$) has one unpaired electron, $\mu$ = 1.73 BM (iii); Ni$^{2+}$ has a d$^8$ configuration (i).

questions.q: Which of the following statements related to lanthanoids is incorrect?
options: Lanthanoids are silvery white soft metals.
Ce$^{+4}$ solutions are widely used as oxidising agents in titrimetric analysis.
Colour of Lanthanoid ion in solution is due to d-d transition.
questions.explanation: The colour of lanthanoid ions arises from f-f transitions, not d-d transitions, making statement D incorrect.

questions.q: A metalloid is:
questions.explanation: Sb and Se are classified as metalloids (as per NCERT's classification for groups 15 and 16).

questions.q: A pair of isoelectronic species having bond order of one is
questions.explanation: O$_2^{2-}$ and F$_2$ each have 18 electrons and, by molecular orbital theory, both have a bond order of 1.

questions.q: Identify the wrong relation for real gases:
questions.explanation: The compressibility factor is defined as $Z = V_{real}/V_{ideal}$, so option A (with the ratio inverted) is the wrong relation.

questions.q: From the diagram A $\xrightarrow{\Delta H_1=+10J}$ 2B $\xrightarrow{\Delta H_2=+25J}$ C. $\Delta_r H$ for the reaction C$\rightarrow$A is:
questions.explanation: A$\rightarrow$C via B has $\Delta H = \Delta H_1+\Delta H_2 = 35$ J, so the reverse reaction C$\rightarrow$A has $\Delta H = -35$ J.

questions.q: For which one of the following mixtures is composition uniform throughout?
questions.explanation: A dilute aqueous sugar solution is a homogeneous mixture, so its composition is uniform throughout.
